When evaluation time comes at the company, they look at how much work the employees did over the course of their last project and they see that coder A wrote 5x as much code. Someone who doesn't understand the less is more philosophy of advanced programming will look at those metrics and just assume that coder A is the harder working, more productive employee. In reality coder B wrote a much cleaner, more stable and easier to use part of the application with those fewer lines, but the people who get to decide pay raises don't understand that, and subsequently the more efficient programmer gets half as large a raise as the "more productive" programmer.
